title: Where do you stand? A check across all six build objectives

items.stem: Your program calls a model through Anthropic's Messages API with "Explain how a torque converter works" and gets a long reply. You now want to ask "Make it shorter." What must your second request contain so the model knows what "it" refers to?

options.text: Only "Make it shorter", because the API keeps the earlier exchange for you
Your first message, the model's reply to it, and then "Make it shorter"
Only "Make it shorter", sent with the same API key so the server links them
Only the model's earlier reply, since that is the text being shortened

items.stem: You write a Python function get_tire_pressure(car) in your own program and describe it to the model as a tool. The model's reply asks to use that tool with car = "Tacoma". What has to happen next for the model to use the reading in its answer?

options.text: Nothing: the model provider runs your function on its servers and the model carries on
Your program runs the function and prints the reading for the user, which ends the turn
Nothing: the model estimates a likely tire pressure itself and carries on
Your program runs the function and sends the reading back to the model in a new request

items.stem: You are building a small research agent that must answer a question about EV battery cooling with citations to pages it actually read. Which set of tools is the smallest that lets it do that?

options.text: A search tool that returns titles and links, and a fetch tool that returns a page's text
A search tool only, since the result snippets are enough to quote and cite
No tools, with an instruction to include a source URL for every claim
A fetch tool only, since the model can recall which URLs to fetch

items.stem: Every morning you want a program to pull the new articles from the same three car-news feeds, summarize each article, and email you the summaries. The steps never change. Which build gives you the most predictable behavior at the lowest cost?

options.text: A full agent with a tool per feed that decides which feeds to read and when to stop
Three agents, one per feed, each running its own loop and reporting to a fourth agent
A fixed workflow: your code runs the steps in order and calls the model once per article
An agent loop whose model picks the order of the feeds and retries any that fail

items.stem: Your agent loop works like this: it calls the model with the task; whenever the model's reply requests tools, your program runs every tool requested in that reply and then calls the model again with all the results; the loop stops when a reply requests no tools. On one task the model's replies are, in order: (1) a request for one web search; (2) a request to fetch three pages, all in that single reply; (3) a request for one more web search; (4) a final answer with no tool requests. How many times does your program call the model in total, counting the first call?
Your research agent's report says "Ceramic brake pads produce less brake dust than semi-metallic pads [3]", where [3] is a link to a page. Which check actually shows that this citation holds up?

options.text: Open the link and confirm it loads and comes from a well-known car website
Open the page and find a passage on it that states the same claim
Ask the agent in a follow-up message whether source [3] supports the claim
Search the claim's wording and confirm other sites say the same thing
